title: Collaboration Equilibrium in Federated Learning

problem.claim: Distributional discrepancies across clients can cause counterproductive consequences in federated collaboration.

gap.claim: Collaborating with all clients does not necessarily achieve the best performance, motivating smaller collaboration coalitions.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces collaboration equilibrium, in which clients collaborate with members that maximally improve learning and isolate those making little contribution.
The paper proposes a benefit graph and a Pareto optimization approach for identifying optimal collaborators.
The paper proves that a collaboration equilibrium can be reached from the benefit graph through an iterative graph operation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning enables collaborative model learning among multiple clients while preserving privacy.
Distributional discrepancies across clients can make collaboration counterproductive, and full participation may not be optimal.
The paper defines collaboration equilibrium, models benefits with a graph, and identifies collaborators through Pareto optimization.
An iterative graph operation is shown to reach a collaboration equilibrium.
Synthetic and real-world experiments are reported as evidence of method effectiveness.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not provide the formal definition, assumptions, or proof details for collaboration equilibrium.
The abstract does not describe the iterative graph operation or its computational complexity.
